○ trial-76o · Return accepted receipt details   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  Add accepted for the current provider protocol. Request:                    
  {"command":"accepted","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional               
  "protocol":"2". Return exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count,   
  and receipts. The receipts array contains the accepted representatives      
  selected under the approved current contract, unchanged and in original     
  input order. Overall counts equal summary for the same request. An empty set
  returns receipts [] and both counts zero. A single input receipt is returned
  unchanged. Existing count and summary versions remain supported.

stdout: Courier Relay protocol 2 receipt identity contract and current-protocol decision. Applies to count and summary (and any later command that dedupes receipts) when "protocol" is omitted or is explicitly "2". Source: provider permanently adopted protocol 2; integration owner approved it as the current protocol in issue trial-3id (approved 2026-09-07, owner csells). Rules: (1) A delivery identity is delivery_id alone, across all accounts; the same delivery_id under another account_id is another receipt of the same delivery. (2) Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: the receipt with the LATEST occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants accept the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. (3) Accepted receipts keep original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order. (4) occurred_at is RFC3339 with seconds, no fractional seconds, Z or explicit numeric offset; compare as UTC instants (offsets may cross a date boundary). (5) The agreement applies to the entire supplied receipt set regardless of receipt dates (2020-2099); no persistence across CLI invocations. Rationale from the provider: delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change it. Protocol selection as of 2026-09-07: omitted "protocol" selects "2" (CURRENT_PROTOCOL in main.py); explicit "2" selects the same contract; explicit "1" keeps the original protocol 1 contract (see courier-relay/protocol-1-receipt-identity); unsupported values return {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. Response shapes unchanged: count and summary return exactly {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count"} reporting the actual protocol used; empty receipts give 0/0; a single receipt gives 1/0. Implemented in main.py (accepted_receipts_v2, ACCEPTED_RECEIPTS, select_protocol); verified 2026-09-07 with public_tests/summary_2.json plus manual cross-account, latest-wins, cross-offset date-boundary tie, and record_id tie cases.

Courier Relay protocol 1 receipt identity and count contract. Applies to the count and summary commands (and any later command that dedupes receipts) when protocol "1" is selected explicitly. Source: vendor/protocol-1.md (provider contract) and issue trial-vsf (approved 2026-09-07, owner csells). Rules: (1) A delivery identity is the pair (account_id, delivery_id); the same delivery_id under a different account_id is a separate delivery. (2) Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: the receipt with the earliest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants accept the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. (3) Accepted receipts keep original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order. (4) occurred_at is RFC3339 with seconds, no fractional seconds, Z or explicit numeric offset; compare as UTC instants (offsets may cross a date boundary). Rationale from the provider: delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change it. Protocol selection: omitted "protocol" selects the current protocol; an explicit supported protocol stays supported after a newer current version is introduced. Public suites name a protocol explicitly. History: protocol 1 was the current protocol from trial-vsf until 2026-09-07, when issue trial-3id made protocol 2 current (see courier-relay/protocol-2-receipt-identity); protocol 1 rules are unchanged and remain supported via explicit "protocol":"1". count response is exactly {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count"}; empty receipts give 0/0; a single receipt gives 1/0. Implemented in main.py (accepted_receipts_v1, select_protocol); verified with public_tests/count_1.json and summary_1.json and manual cross-offset and tie cases on 2026-09-07.

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  The provider has permanently adopted protocol 2, and the integration owner  
  approved using it as the current protocol. The complete new contract is:    
                                                                              
  Protocol 2: delivery_id alone identifies a delivery across all accounts; the
  same ID under another account is another receipt of that delivery. Exactly  
  one receipt is accepted per delivery identity. Accept the receipt with the  
  latest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants use the smallest record_id.  
  All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. Each accepted receipt  
  retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload. Present       
  accepted receipts in their original input order. This identity contract     
  comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account         
  attribution alone does not change that guarantee.                           
                                                                              
  Update count and summary so omitted protocol selects "2" and explicit       
  "protocol":"2" selects the same agreement. Explicit protocol "1" keeps the  
  original provider contract. Shapes are unchanged; report the actual protocol
  used. The new agreement applies to the entire supplied set regardless of    
  receipt dates. Empty sets have zero counts; one receipt has one accepted and
  zero duplicates.
